notes.title: Dev Diary #9
notes.notes: [h3]Hi everyone, it's time to share some news with you, the first news since I started reworking my game.[/h3][h3][/h3][p]First of all, I wanted to rework the very concept of the game, to make a simulation where the player himself builds a club as he wants and almost anywhere he wants. Mechanics went more towards strategy and management, but it will not make the game more stuffy, and I would say even on the contrary. I have plans to make a game where you can relax, and in this respect I think I hit the mark. To all the pluses I can add more variability and even more elements that the player can control. For example, optimizing the flow of visitors, expanding rooms, managing resources such as drink stocks, etc.[/p][p][/p][p]At the moment the construction system has been implemented. Now you can build a club as you want, any shape and any size (within the map). Partially realized the system of tasks for the staff. Further I plan to finish the construction system completely and will start to realize the visitors in the club.[/p][p][/p][p]And now I'm done, thanks for following the project and see you in the next diary![/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #8
notes.notes: [p][b]Hi everyone, welcome to the new developer diary. In this issue I will share new details, problems and plans about my game.[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]The main problem.[/b][/h3][p]I really like the simulation genre. Interesting and addictive games are released in this genre. [/p][p]And with my game I would like to bring something interesting to this genre too. My game is about managing a nightclub and I want the player to feel like the manager of the club, its creator and owner. Not just some handyman who inherited a club in the suburbs and now the player has to improve it. I want to do something more directed towards the creation of something of its own and management of resources, personnel and finances.[/p][p]At the very beginning of development I had already made one of the most important decisions, to make the game in low poly style. To make stylized graphics, which will not be similar to other projects in this genre. So now I want to make a second important decision, to give the project a second life.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Further development.[/b][/h3][p]I wondered why game development was going so hard. At that moment I realized that I was doing the wrong thing, trying to do everything according to some formula that I didn't like.[/p][p]So now, based on the current game I will be making multiple edits to the gameplay and generally reworking some aspects of the game.[/p][p]The game is still alive and I'll still be sharing development news. I'm still working alone and I apologize for any delays and moments in the middle of development.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Thank you for following the project, see you in the next developer diary![/b][/p]

notes.title: Beta announcement!
notes.notes: [h3]Hi everyone, it's time to announce the launch of the beta version of my game.[/h3][p][/p][p]I decided to first give you, so to speak, to try out my game. And based on your feedback I want to gradually improve it and go to the full release. As a beta version I will launch a demo version in Steam. That way I can collect more feedback from players.[/p][p][/p][p]Now I've switched my focus to making this demo version and I'll put it on the page soon. I've also started making a discord server for easy feedback gathering and in general to create a whole community.[/p][p][/p][p]I'm still working on the game alone and it's very hard to keep track of all aspects. So the demo version will be released this summer.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for following the project! See you in the next post.[/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #7
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, it's past time to share news about the development of my game.

This time I would like to mention the delays in development. In recent testing some flaws and defects in the basic mechanics of the game were discovered. Because of this I had to spend more time on development and finalization than planned.

But there are a lot of positives in this. I slightly reworked the game's setting, moving the game's action to a tropical island. I wanted to add something unusual to my project. Where is the nightclub usually located? In back alleys, somewhere in skyscrapers or underground, it's all interesting, but I considered adding an island to be something unusual, something out of the ordinary. In addition to this there can be more immersed in the party atmosphere and such a summer vibe.

Testers found some inconsistency in the game models. Some items and effects are knocked out of the overall game. Therefore, some time will have to be spent on polishing the game models and effects.

One more important thing, I added support for Steam cloud save. reworked the save system in the game to a more advanced system, which works better and is suitable for Steam cloud save.

Now my personal findings. The way the player interacts with items, such as lifting them or carrying them, I found it very clumsy. So I made some changes that capture even the mechanics of the bar and interaction with NPCs. Adding the bar tray made the game feel different, customer service became a bit more enjoyable, and overall it looks better than just a glass levitating in the air.

There were also minor changes like new color correction, polishing existing mechanics, and creating a more user-friendly UI.

That's about it for me. Thanks for following the projects and see you in the next post!

notes.title: Dev Diary #6
notes.notes:
[h3]Hi everyone! In this diary I would like to share my progress since the release of the last diary. I am very pleased with the fact that I have been very productive. [/h3]

I have done a lot of work on optimizing the game and the project as a whole. I have redone several systems such as: building system, delivery system, improved online stores, improved NPC behavior system, and improved the ordering system.

I also want to note the improvements in feedback from the game, it became feel and play much better thanks to new animations and some assets.

At the moment I'm working on the quest system, which I made this week, and I'm also planning to start developing the story for the game.

This time I was surprised to see that there were no major difficulties and the process went very quickly. So I hope to publish the game in full access very soon.

[h3]Thanks for following the project![/h3]

notes.title: Dev Diary #5
notes.notes:
[h3]It's been a while since the last devlog was released, so today I'm sharing game development news again.[/h3]

First off, I'd like to start by noting the release date of the game.
I have plans to finish development by summer. At this point the game is almost ready, all that's left to do is finalize a few important mechanics and polish the game. I really want to publish the game already, but every time I have to postpone the release. I'm working on another project as a programmer and now I don't have enough time to develop my own game. But nevertheless I try to give time for my game as much as possible. 

To the slowing down of the pace of development I started restructuring my game. I started cleaning up code, scenes, unnecessary mechanics, prefabs and so on. When a project is a mess, it becomes very difficult to continue development. That's why I'm spending the last time on polishing the existing mechanics and restructuring the project.

Now about what I realized. I improved the system and the code of the NPS, namely improved the queue system, the logic of order selection and logic in general and optimized the code because before it was very much affected the performance. Made a new bar system. To pour drinks is not boring and in general was interesting I made a whole mini game, in the future I want to improve it a little more. Added a new location for the club, as well as the ability to choose the original location and type of club.

I won't add a lot of minor corrections and will focus on the most important points. So that's it, thanks for following the project!

notes.title: Dev Diary #4
notes.notes:
Hi, welcome to the new developer diary.

Since the last issue, I've been focusing on improving the game's feel and balance. During this period, I've reworked a few key mechanics:

[list]
[*] Improved the bar and drink pouring system, making the process smoother and more intuitive.
[*] Revamped the DJ work, improving the music and interaction with the sound.
[*] Updated the dance floor mechanics and visitor behavior.
[/list]

However, in the process of making the changes, some bugs arose that I'm actively working on now. This required rewriting several standard engine scripts to ensure stability and improve performance.

Thank you for following the development of the game!

notes.title: Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hi! The last few days of development have not been very productive, I've been very busy, but I'm trying to spend as much time as possible on game development.

The other day I thought about it and realized that the game is wrong, namely the game does not honor the development of the character and the club itself. It feels like everything is already there at the start. So I decided to redo some aspects of the game. I started to do it rather late, because in less than 3 weeks the game should be ready. But I'm still hoping for the best, namely that I will be able to realize everything by the release date of the game.

Now for the little things. I improved the UI in the game, added more music, and also made a store, just like in the recently popular game Supermarket Simulator. Plus improved NPCs and hiring system.
The plan is to add something like entertainment for the player himself, such as games within the game or any activity. I also think it will be good to give the opportunity to put their music in the club, but this is already as it turns out.

That's all I have, have a nice day!

notes.title: Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Greetings, in this new diary I would like to talk about drug trading in my game.

I play a lot of games and have spent a lot of time in games like GTA Online and Drug Dealer Simulator. The latter is very addictive and at one time I only played it. So the main mechanics in DDS was respectively trading drugs, and in GTA Online there is also a nightclub where you can do such things. So these two games inspired me to create this kind of activity in my game.

I have a problem with the game being repetitive, short, boring and I thought it would be a good idea to add such mechanics to the game. There's another cool game called Drug Lord Tycoon. In it as it is not difficult to guess the player is doing what trades substances, but such a process there is made as I think on excellent. First you need to grow a “plant”, watch its humidity, then dry it and find a dealer to sell it. This is only for one type of drug. The description may not be the most interesting, but believe me it's addictive.

So in my game it should look good and dilute the gameplay a bit.
Adding this activity will add a lot of random events, which I really love in all games. This kind of random events will also diversify the gameplay and so to say the player's life.

That's all I have for now. All the best to you!

notes.title: Developer's Diary #1
notes.notes:
Greetings, everyone! This is my first developer diary where I would like to share the development process of my game.

This is my first experience in creating a relatively large game and my first experience in writing a diary. 
I'm 16 years old and an aspiring game developer, I've always been inspired by indie developers and their games, successful and not so successful. Partly because of this I will start a diary like this, I'm very curious to see how it turns out and if it turns out at all, but I will try, learn and doing something new is always a good thing.

And now to the game itself. I plan to put it in full access on February 25, the development is in full swing, but almost every day there are different difficulties, from bugs in the game itself to my burnout from these bugs. It happens that a system that is supposed to work doesn't work or something breaks. The latest such problem was a problem with saves. I used a tool that I bought at the Asset Store. At first everything was fine, the tool is very handy and works well, but then when using it began to appear an error that completely froze all the development of the game. I wrote to the developer of this tool and it turned out that nobody had this error, the developer himself did not know why it appeared. 2 weeks later, I got tired of trying to solve the error, so to speak, freaked out and wrote my own save tool that works in conjunction with the old one.

Kudos to the developer of the main tool anyway for the quick replies, his asset is still cool and I like it a lot.
I don't know how this diary came about, but it's a good experience for me, especially since I've never written anything like this on the net. All the best to you!
